Original decision description: What is the intended operational boundary and who is the railway authority for this system?
Recommended disposition: Project owner to scope this release as an offline, non-operational solver-comparison experiment only; no operational authority or approval is implied.
Rationale: Purpose, research question, and prototype disclaimer are project scope decisions. Any move to planning support or operational control still requires external authority and a separate safety lifecycle.
Who must approve it: Project owner; external railway operations and safety authority for any expanded scope
Blocks proposed prototype: Yes, until offline-only scope is approved

Original decision description: Which infrastructure registry and version define segments, sections, lines, directions, routes, and assets?
Recommended disposition: Do not create a real topology. Use current code-defined section/line labels only as synthetic simulation keys, visibly labeled unverified.
Rationale: Current route sections and binary line enum do not establish physical infrastructure or versioned topology.
Who must approve it: Infrastructure owner / railway authority
Blocks proposed prototype: No for bounded synthetic comparison; yes for topology-dependent extension

Original decision description: How are logical adjacency, shared assets, junctions, crossovers, and conflict groups defined?
Recommended disposition: Do not infer adjacency operationally. Retain the solver's current label-based adjacent-line case only as a prototype behavior, not an approved rule.
Rationale: Logical adjacency is an infrastructure/operating relationship, not derivable from line names or proximity.
Who must approve it: Infrastructure, operations, and safety authorities
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current-model research; yes for adjacent-resource operational claims

Original decision description: What geometry/chainage reference, accuracy, uncertainty and conversion defines a worksite and train footprint?
Recommended disposition: Treat current route interpolation and optional km endpoints as unvalidated simulation geometry only; no operational distance conclusion.
Rationale: No verified chainage registry, CRS, or worksite geometry is present.
Who must approve it: Infrastructure and data-governance owners; safety owner for use in safety checks
Blocks proposed prototype: No for simulation; yes for spatial verification work

Original decision description: What buffer, equipment envelope, measurement method, boundary equality, and uncertainty policy apply to each work/activity combination?
Recommended disposition: Do not adopt the verifier's current 1,000 m / 2,000 m constants as railway standards. Keep them explicitly labeled code assumptions or disable operational interpretation.
Rationale: The source code is the only evidence for current values; no approved standard/source was established.
Who must approve it: Railway safety and infrastructure authorities
Blocks proposed prototype: No for solver-only synthetic experiments; yes for any safety-clearance claim

Original decision description: Which timetable/movement provider is authoritative for each route, operating date, and movement class?
Recommended disposition: Use the bundled timetable solely as a fixed, non-authoritative benchmark input; do not make a completeness or safety claim.
Rationale: Dataset presence, row count, or custom upload does not authenticate source or completeness.
Who must approve it: Railway operations and timetable data-governance owners
Blocks proposed prototype: No for existing-data experiments; yes for verified clearance

Original decision description: What exactly constitutes complete timetable coverage and how is freshness established?
Recommended disposition: Keep coverage evidence UNKNOWN unless a real provider and scoped completeness protocol are approved and integrated.
Rationale: Default EvidenceProvider authenticates nothing; source labels are caller-controlled.
Who must approve it: Railway operations, data governance, safety
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current simulation; yes for verified schedule status

Original decision description: What operating-date, time-zone, service-day, overnight, and clock-change semantics apply?
Recommended disposition: Constrain current experiment to the existing 0–24 hour simulation horizon, clearly not a date-qualified operating timetable.
Rationale: Raw CSV lacks an established service date/time zone; app uses hour-of-day values and ignores days_of_week in window derivation.
Who must approve it: Railway operations and timetable data owner
Blocks proposed prototype: No for fixed-horizon research; yes for dated operational scheduling

Original decision description: How are cancellations, delays, diversions, unscheduled trains, missed updates, and feed corrections represented and propagated?
Recommended disposition: No live updates or schedule-currentness claims in the prototype; treat a benchmark instance as immutable input snapshot.
Rationale: No update feed, revocation lifecycle, or freshness protocol exists.
Who must approve it: Railway operations, timetable provider, safety
Blocks proposed prototype: No for offline experiment; yes for use of a schedule after data changes

Original decision description: What work activities require a possession, closure, movement restriction, or other operational authority, and who grants it?
Recommended disposition: Do not represent solver time blocks as possessions, closures, or releases. Exclude operational authorization from the prototype.
Rationale: No authority-grant or possession workflow exists, and a planned interval is not an operational grant.
Who must approve it: Railway operations and safety authorities; maintenance owner
Blocks proposed prototype: No for simulation; operational authorization remains out of scope

Original decision description: What traction/electrical assets, isolation scope, state and authorized confirmation source apply to each job?
Recommended disposition: Preserve fail-closed verifier behavior; no traction work may be represented as operationally verified from Boolean/source fields.
Rationale: No circuit-level data or authenticated isolation provider exists.
Who must approve it: Electrical/traction authority and safety owner
Blocks proposed prototype: No for solver comparison; yes for traction verification

Original decision description: What worksite-protection arrangements and evidence are required for each task class?
Recommended disposition: Do not invent protection procedures or infer approval; label the verifier as a limited prototype checker.
Rationale: Project contains no protection plan or authority-defined activity catalogue.
Who must approve it: Railway operations and safety authority; maintenance owner
Blocks proposed prototype: No for solver-only experiment; yes for safety verification

Original decision description: Which maintenance task taxonomy maps work types to qualifications, equipment, possession/isolation needs, and conflict rules?
Recommended disposition: Keep current defect_type labels synthetic/descriptive; do not infer task-specific requirements from them.
Rationale: Current free-text defect labels are not a validated operational taxonomy.
Who must approve it: Maintenance and safety authorities
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current solver comparison; yes for task-rule implementation

Original decision description: How should maintenance priority trade against aggregate work-order coverage?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: For research only, report current urgency values as synthetic ordering metadata; do not claim a priority policy or change the objective without project-owner approval.
Rationale: The urgency enum is generated and currently affects search ordering but is not a binding priority objective. Operational priority requires external policy.
Who must approve it: Project owner for simulation assumption; maintenance/operations authority for any real priority semantics
Blocks proposed prototype: No for baseline comparison; yes for a priority-optimization claim

Original decision description: What lexicographic order should disruption, schedule stability, workload balance, utilization, and co-location follow after hard feasibility and coverage?
Recommended disposition: Approve a research-only metric hierarchy and report each metric separately; do not modify current solver objective in this scope.

Who must approve it: Project owner for experimental evaluation; railway operations/maintenance for operational objectives
Blocks proposed prototype: Yes for new objective-quality conclusions; not for reporting current objectives separately

Original decision description: How is train/service disruption measured and which movements/services may be affected?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: Use only the current solver time-of-day/train-gap score as a named prototype proxy; do not call it service disruption.
Rationale: Current proxy is calculable from supplied windows but not a validated delay or service-impact measure.
Who must approve it: Project owner for labeled proxy; operations/timetable authority for real disruption cost
Blocks proposed prototype: No for solver run comparison; yes for operational disruption claims

Original decision description: Which crew pools, credentials, validity rules, availability, capacity and historical duty data may be used?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: Do not add real crew claims. Later, synthetic crew counts/calendars may support isolated algorithm tests if every value is labeled artificial and no qualification/operational claim is made.
Rationale: No crew/qualification data exists; synthetic resource fixtures can test generic capacity logic but not staff feasibility.
Who must approve it: Project owner for synthetic fixtures; external workforce/credential and safety owners for real data/policy
Blocks proposed prototype: No for present model; yes for resource-extended simulation

Original decision description: What equipment types, quantities, capacities, compatibility, maintenance state and movement envelopes apply?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: Keep existing heavy_equipment Boolean as a model input only. Synthetic equipment inventory may be used later for algorithm tests, never as a railway inventory.
Rationale: The Boolean does not identify equipment or provide capacity/compatibility; no inventory exists.
Who must approve it: Project owner for synthetic fixtures; maintenance/infrastructure authority for real inventory/rules
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current comparison; yes for equipment-capacity simulation

Original decision description: What travel, access, mobilization, setup, dismantling, and transition-time model is approved?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: Do not infer travel from section IDs. Later synthetic transition matrices may test solver support and must be clearly artificial.
Rationale: No travel or access network/time model is present; a simulation can test generic transition constraints without claiming actual reachability.
Who must approve it: Project owner for synthetic fixtures; operations/infrastructure/maintenance for real model
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current comparison; yes for travel-constraint experiment

Original decision description: Which shift, duty, break, maximum-work and rest policies apply, with what rolling horizon and history?
Recommended disposition: Do not implement legal or operational duty/rest rules from current 8-hour objective buckets. A separate generic synthetic calendar may be proposed only under an explicit test fixture decision.
Rationale: Duty/rest rules and historic crew data require policy authority; objective buckets are not working-hour limits.
Who must approve it: Workforce policy, maintenance, safety authorities
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current comparison; yes for real crew-feasibility claims

Original decision description: How are work durations estimated, including uncertainty, setup, contingency, phases, interruptions, and restart costs?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: Use current fixed synthetic duration_hrs for historical-model reproduction only. Future distributions or interruption cases require labeled synthetic assumptions and must not be interpreted as work estimates.
Rationale: Current durations are generated from fixed tiers and solver assumes one non-preemptive interval.
Who must approve it: Project owner for synthetic model; maintenance/engineering/operations for real estimates
Blocks proposed prototype: No for reproducing existing model; yes for robust-duration research

Original decision description: Which earliest starts, latest completions, hard deadlines, preferred windows, and calendar exceptions apply per work order?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: No real windows/deadlines are implied. Later synthetic windows can test algorithm behavior, with explicit fixture labels and no operational priority claim.
Rationale: These fields are absent. Artificial values can test constraints only if kept separate from real data.
Who must approve it: Project owner for synthetic fixtures; maintenance/operations authorities for actual windows
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current comparison; yes for window/deadline extension

Original decision description: What dependency types, lag, predecessor state, waiver authority, and cycle semantics apply?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: A future generic precedence graph can be used for synthetic solver tests; it must not be populated from defect descriptions or treated as actual job sequencing.
Rationale: No dependency data exists; generic graph fixtures test implementation but not engineering sequence policy.
Who must approve it: Project owner for synthetic fixtures; maintenance/engineering authority for real dependencies
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current comparison; yes for dependency experiment

Original decision description: When may tasks co-locate, and what shared access, crew, equipment, possession and protection conditions are required?
Category: C. Project decision possible only as an explicit simulation assumption
Recommended disposition: For historical reproduction, document the current bilateral flag/exact-window rule as a legacy model assumption. Any new synthetic policy must be explicit; no co-location is operationally approved.
Rationale: Current `co_location_allowed` is a synthetic Boolean and exact same-window exception, without shared-site/resource evidence.
Who must approve it: Project owner for simulation; maintenance/operations/safety authorities for real co-location
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current comparison; yes for revised co-location policy

Original decision description: What solver outcome, proof state, partial output, unscheduled reason, and API-status semantics are canonical?
Recommended disposition: Use separate coverage, termination, proof, and safety dimensions in research reports; preserve existing API and solver behavior in this documentation-only task.
Rationale: Solver/API contract semantics and truthful presentation are software project decisions; no project semantics may claim railway approval.
Who must approve it: Project owner; operations review for operator-facing language
Blocks proposed prototype: Yes before future solver/API integration or operator-oriented presentation

Original decision description: What evidence states, applicability rules, audit denominator, retention, and revocation behavior are required?
Recommended disposition: Do not redefine production verification. Keep the existing fail-closed evidence boundary; operational evidence semantics and retention require railway safety/data governance approval.
Rationale: Evidence types and safety applicability depend on authority; current Boolean/null audit is only prototype behavior.
Who must approve it: Railway safety, data governance, application owner
Blocks proposed prototype: No for solver-only research; yes for changing verified status/compliance semantics

Original decision description: What data retention, privacy, security, access control, and auditability apply to work, timetable, crew, and safety evidence?
Recommended disposition: Do not ingest actual operational, staff, or safety records without applicable governance approval. Use only already bundled public/synthetic data for this experiment.
Rationale: Future data may be sensitive; neither public availability nor a prototype grants rights to process external records.
Who must approve it: Data governance, security, railway authority
Blocks proposed prototype: No for current public/synthetic experiment; yes before external-data integration

Original decision description: What schedule-change events invalidate a prior result, and who can re-authorize it?
Recommended disposition: Do not support schedule reuse or claim current validity in this offline experiment. Operational invalidation/re-authorisation needs authority-defined lifecycle.
Rationale: No event integration or evidence lifecycle exists; invalidation authority is operational.
Who must approve it: Operations, safety, data governance
Blocks proposed prototype: No for immutable offline instance research; yes for persistent schedule lifecycle

Original decision description: Which proof requirements must be met before presenting an objective as optimal or coverage as maximum?
Recommended disposition: Adopt proof-specific reporting language: incumbent, complete feasible, coverage proven, objective proven, and unknown/limit are separate. Do not equate complete schedule with optimality.
Rationale: Proof-reporting criteria and claim discipline are project-owned; certificates remain limited to the exact encoded model.
Who must approve it: Project owner; model owner
Blocks proposed prototype: Yes for defensible research claims
Blocks operational use: Yes for any optimality or maximum-coverage claim

Recommended disposition: For this prototype, use the bundled CSV as fixed non-authoritative schedule input and deterministic synthetic orders (at most the available 90) for simulation only; future generated scenarios must be labeled synthetic.
Rationale: Current benchmark uses synthetic work orders and shared timetable windows. Governed operational data requires external authorization; simulation design can be selected by project owner.
